newsitem.title: ITALY: Zaire gives UN chief agreement to aid effort.
newsitem.headline: Zaire gives UN chief agreement to aid effort.

text.p: Zaire's Prime Minister Leon Kengo wa Dondo told U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali on Monday his government was willing to help the U.N. get aid to refugees in eastern Zaire, a spokeswoman for Boutros-Ghali said.
Kengo made the pledge in a lengthy telephone conversation with Boutros-Ghali, who is in Rome for this week's World Food Summit, spokeswoman Therese Gastaut said in a statement.

The statement said Boutros-Ghali welcomed the undertaking and hoped for rapid results while continuing to believe a multinational force would be needed in the area, where fighting threatens more than a million refugees from Rwanda and Burundi.

"The Secretary-General said there had been a positive exchange of views, with (Kengo) declaring his willingness to cooperate with the United Nations to facilitate the provision of humanitarian assistance," the statement said.

It said the U.N. Coordinator of Humanitarian Assistance for the Great Lakes Region, Sergio Vieira de Mello, who is in Kinshasa, would meet senior Zairean officials to arrange details of delivering humanitarian assistance to eastern Zaire.

"The Secretary-General hopes these efforts will bring quick results but recognises that the extreme security situation demands a multinational force in the region to create conditions for a humanitarian operation," the statement said.
